name: Momentum crash gate: 12-1 momentum scaled down in bear + high-vol states (Daniel-Moskowitz)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 505. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1 for each eligible name; pick the top 20% by mom. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). bear = (product of (1+EW market daily return) over the last 504 days) - 1 < 0. highVol = annualised std of EW market daily returns over the last 126 days > 0.25. scale s = 1 if neither, 0.5 if exactly one, 0 if both. Weight = s/N on each picked name, rest cash.
rationale: Momentum's worst months cluster after bear markets when volatility is high (the 'momentum crash'); Daniel and Moskowitz show that de-risking in those states roughly doubles the strategy Sharpe.
source: Daniel & Moskowitz 2016, 'Momentum crashes', Journal of Financial Economics 122(2), 221-247

name: Market-state momentum: 12-1 momentum only after a positive 24-month market (Cooper-Gutierrez-Hameed)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 505. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1; top 20% by mom. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). UP state = cumulative EW market return over the last 504 days > 0. If UP: equal-weight the picked names; else hold cash (weights {}).
rationale: Momentum profits appear only following up markets, consistent with overconfidence-driven overreaction that needs a prior run-up; in down states momentum is flat to negative.
source: Cooper, Gutierrez & Hameed 2004, 'Market states and momentum', Journal of Finance 59(3), 1345-1365

name: Jegadeesh-Titman 6/6 overlapping momentum (six monthly cohorts, 1-week skip)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 260. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. At rebalance t, for k = 0..5 let tk = t - 21*k (a bar-index offset within each name's own bars: tk = lastIndex - 21*k). Cohort k = top 20% of eligible names by close[tk-5]/close[tk-126] - 1 (ranked using only bars up to tk). Final weight(sym) = sum over k of (1/6) * (1/Nk) for each cohort k containing sym.
rationale: The original formation-6/holding-6 design with overlapping portfolios is the canonical momentum test; most later tests use 12-1, so whether JT's own 6/6 still works in large caps is an open, often-asked question.
source: Jegadeesh & Titman 1993, 'Returns to buying winners and selling losers', Journal of Finance 48(1), 65-91
prereg_note: prereg: tk defined as a per-name bar-index offset.

name: Fresh momentum: recent winners whose prior six months were losers (Chen-Kadan-Kose)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. recent = close[t-21]/close[t-126] - 1; prior = close[t-126]/close[t-252] - 1. U = top 30% of eligible names by recent. Among U, long the half (floor(|U|/2) names) with the LOWEST prior (the freshest winners). Equal weight.
rationale: Momentum that has just begun ('fresh') is not yet crowded and has further to run, whereas 'stale' winners whose run began a year ago are closer to reversal.
source: Chen, Kadan & Kose 2009, 'Fresh momentum', working paper (Washington University in St. Louis), SSRN 1374057

name: Absolute strength momentum: long only when 12-1 return clears a fixed historical percentile (Gulen-Petkova)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1. Keep an expanding pool (in ctx.state) of every eligible name's mom at every past rebalance date. Once the pool holds >= 24 rebalance dates, threshold = 90th percentile of the pool (computed from past rebalances only, then append the current cross-section after deciding). Long every name with mom >= threshold, equal weight; cash if none.
rationale: Relative (cross-sectional) momentum forces a long book even when nothing is going up; absolute-strength winners (strong versus history, not peers) are the ones that actually continue, and the exposure naturally drops in weak markets.
source: Gulen & Petkova 2018, 'Absolute strength: exploring momentum in stock returns', working paper (Purdue / Rice), SSRN 2638004

name: Capital gains overhang: unrealised-gain proxy from a volume-weighted reference price (Grinblatt-Han)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 270. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. Reference price RP = sum over n=1..260 of w_n*close[t-n] / sum w_n, with w_n = volume[t-n] * (1-0.0167)^n (volume-weighted, decaying with age as a stand-in for turnover). CGO = close[t-5]/RP - 1. Long the top 20% by CGO, equal weight.
rationale: Disposition-effect investors sell winners sitting on paper gains, which depresses the price below fundamental value and creates predictable continuation; Grinblatt and Han show the overhang, not past return per se, drives momentum.
source: Grinblatt & Han 2005, 'Prospect theory, mental accounting, and momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 78(2), 311-339

name: Recency of the 52-week high: near the high AND the high was set recently (Bhootra-Hur)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. near = close[t] / max(high[t-251..t]); daysSince = t - argmax index of that high. Filter F = top 50% of eligible names by near. Among F, long the 20% of the FULL universe count (0.2*N_eligible names) with the smallest daysSince (recency ratio (252-daysSince)/252 closest to 1). Equal weight.
rationale: Anchoring on the 52-week high is strongest when the high is recent: investors under-react to news that has just pushed a stock to a new high, so recent-high stocks outperform old-high stocks at the same nearness.
source: Bhootra & Hur 2013, 'The timing of 52-week high price and momentum', Journal of Banking & Finance 37(10), 3773-3782

name: Value-and-momentum combo across asset-class ETFs (Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen 'everywhere')
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = the 25 discovery ETFs, eligible if bars > 757. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1; value = -(close[t]/close[t-756] - 1) (3-year reversal; AMP use 5 years, shortened for data). Cross-sectional percentile ranks r_mom, r_val in [0,1]; score = 0.5*r_mom + 0.5*r_val. Long the top min(6, N_eligible) by score, weight 1/6 each (so under 1 when fewer than 6 are eligible); cash if none eligible.
rationale: Momentum and (long-horizon reversal) value are negatively correlated, so their equal combination has a much higher Sharpe than either alone, a pattern AMP document in every asset class they examine.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013, 'Value and momentum everywhere', Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985
prereg_note: prereg: fewer-than-6-eligible case defined.

name: Value-and-momentum combo in stocks (12-1 momentum + 24-month reversal skipping 12)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 757. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1; value = -(close[t-252]/close[t-756] - 1) (return from 36 to 12 months ago, negated). Percentile ranks r_mom, r_val; score = 0.5*r_mom + 0.5*r_val. Long the top 20% by score, equal weight.
rationale: Price-only value (long-run reversal) and momentum hedge each other's crashes; AMP show the 50/50 blend dominates each leg in US stocks.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013, 'Value and momentum everywhere', Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985; De Bondt & Thaler 1985 for the reversal leg

name: Conservative formula, price-only: low 3-year volatility then high 12-1 momentum (Blitz-van Vliet)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 757. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. vol = std of daily returns over the last 756 bars. Universe half H = the 50% of eligible names with the lowest vol. Among H, long the names with the highest close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1, taking 0.2*N_eligible names. Equal weight.
rationale: Low-vol stocks have the anomaly's return with less risk, and sorting them by momentum avoids the value traps among them; the payout-yield leg is dropped here, so this isolates the vol+momentum part of the formula.
source: Blitz & van Vliet 2018, 'The conservative formula: quantitative investing made easy', Journal of Portfolio Management 44(7), 24-38

name: Crypto one-week cross-sectional momentum, weekly (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu r1,0)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 8. score = close[t]/close[t-7] - 1. k = max(3, floor(0.3*N_eligible)); cash if N_eligible < 3. Long the top k by score, equal weight.
rationale: Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu find one-, two-, three- and four-week momentum all priced in the crypto cross-section; only the 3- and 4-week horizons have been tested here, so the shortest horizon is the open one.
source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, 'Common risk factors in cryptocurrency', Journal of Finance 77(2), 1133-1177
prereg_note: prereg: 'min 3' made explicit.

name: Crypto low realised volatility, weekly (low-vol anomaly test in the LTW cross-section)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 31. vol = std of the last 30 daily returns. Long the 6 lowest-vol names, weight 1/6 each (k = min(6, N_eligible) names at 1/k each; cash if N_eligible < 3).
rationale: The low-volatility anomaly is one of the most robust in equities; Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu report volatility is NOT priced in crypto, so this is a direct replication of a published null that practitioners keep asking about.
source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, 'Common risk factors in cryptocurrency', Journal of Finance 77(2); Baker, Bradley & Wurgler 2011, 'Benchmarks as limits to arbitrage', FAJ 67(1)
prereg_note: prereg: fewer-eligible case made explicit.

name: Sector ETF low volatility: hold the 3 least volatile of 11 sectors, monthly
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 11 sector ETFs, eligible if bars > 61. vol = std of the last 60 daily returns. Long the 3 lowest-vol sectors, weight 1/3 each.
rationale: Benchmark-constrained managers overpay for high-beta sectors, so the low-vol sectors earn similar returns with less risk; at the sector level this is the 'defensive' tilt tested without stock-specific noise.
source: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler 2011, 'Benchmarks as limits to arbitrage: understanding the low-volatility anomaly', Financial Analysts Journal 67(1), 40-54

name: Betting against beta across asset-class ETFs, long low-beta leg weighted by 1/beta (Frazzini-Pedersen)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 25 discovery ETFs (QQQ is the market proxy, proxyFor SPY), eligible if bars > 253. For each ETF: beta_raw = corr(ETF daily ret, QQQ daily ret over 252 bars) * std(ETF)/std(QQQ) over the same 252 bars; beta = 0.6*beta_raw + 0.4*1. Long the min(8, N_eligible) ETFs with the lowest beta (QQQ itself may be chosen), weight_i = (1/beta_i) / sum_j(1/beta_j) over the 8 (sum = 1, never levered; if any beta <= 0.05 clamp it to 0.05).
rationale: Leverage-constrained investors bid up high-beta assets, so low-beta assets have higher risk-adjusted returns; FP show the effect across asset classes, and the 1/beta weighting is their un-levered long leg.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen 2014, 'Betting against beta', Journal of Financial Economics 111(1), 1-25
prereg_note: prereg: fewer-eligible case defined.

name: Sector dual momentum: top 3 sectors by 12-month return, each held only if it beats SHY (Antonacci)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 11 sectors + AGG + SHY, eligible if bars > 253. r12(x) = close[t]/close[t-252] - 1. Rank the 11 sectors by r12; take the top 3. For each of the 3 slots (1/3 weight): hold the sector if r12(sector) > hurdle, else put that slot in AGG, where hurdle = r12(SHY) if SHY is eligible else 0. Slots with no eligible sector go to AGG; if AGG is not eligible either, that slot is cash. SHY is never held (reference only); AGG receives the failed slots.
rationale: Relative momentum picks the leaders and absolute momentum (versus the T-bill proxy) steps aside in bear markets; Antonacci shows the combination cuts drawdowns far more than either alone.
source: Antonacci 2014, 'Dual Momentum Investing' (McGraw-Hill), ch. 8; Antonacci 2013, 'Absolute momentum: a simple rule-based strategy and universal trend-following overlay', SSRN 2244633
prereg_note: prereg: SHY/AGG-not-yet-eligible and fewer-than-3-sectors cases defined (AGG/QQQ-era history starts 2005, sectors 2016).

name: Commodity dual momentum: top 2 of GLD/SLV/USO/DBC/UNG by 12-month return, else SHY (Antonacci)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = GLD SLV USO DBC UNG SHY, eligible if bars > 253. r12 = close[t]/close[t-252] - 1. Rank the 5 commodity ETFs by r12, take the top 2, each a 1/2 slot. A slot holds its commodity only if r12(commodity) > hurdle, hurdle = r12(SHY) if SHY is eligible else 0; otherwise the slot holds SHY (cash if SHY is not eligible). Slots with no eligible commodity are treated as failed slots.
rationale: Commodity ETFs have long, deep bear markets (contango bleed) that relative momentum alone rides down; the absolute-momentum filter against the bill rate is designed to sit those out.
source: Antonacci 2014, 'Dual Momentum Investing' (McGraw-Hill), ch. 8; Miffre & Rallis 2007, 'Momentum strategies in commodity futures markets', JBF 31(6)
prereg_note: prereg: SHY-not-yet-eligible case defined (GLD history starts 2005, SHY 2016).

name: Bond dual momentum: best of HYG/LQD/TLT by 12-month return, held only if it beats SHY (Antonacci)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = HYG LQD TLT SHY, eligible if bars > 253. r12 = close[t]/close[t-252] - 1. Winner = argmax r12 over {HYG, LQD, TLT}. Hold weight 1.0 in the winner if r12(winner) > r12(SHY), else weight 1.0 in SHY.
rationale: Credit and duration alternate leadership across the cycle and both suffer identifiable bear phases; Antonacci's bond module uses the same relative-then-absolute rule and reports strong risk-adjusted results.
source: Antonacci 2014, 'Dual Momentum Investing' (McGraw-Hill), ch. 8 ('Dual momentum in fixed income'); Jostova, Nikolova, Philipov & Stahel 2013, 'Momentum in corporate bond returns', RFS 26(7)

name: Short-horizon time-series momentum: 1-month lookback, 1-month hold, 25 ETFs, long-only (MOP 2012)
rule: signal() mode, daily bars. On the first bar of each UTC calendar month (ymd(t) month differs from ymd(bars[i-1].time) month) compute r = close[i]/close[i-21] - 1 and set ctx.state.pos = r > 0 ? 1 : 0. Return ctx.state.pos every bar (0 before 21 bars of history).
rationale: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen report positive time-series momentum at the 1-month horizon in every asset class; the 12-month version has been tested here, the short horizon has not.
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012, 'Time series momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250 (Table 2, k=1 lookback)

name: Crypto 3-month time-series momentum, monthly check, long-only (MOP horizon test in crypto)
rule: signal() mode, daily bars. On the first bar of each UTC calendar month compute r = close[i]/close[i-90] - 1 and set ctx.state.pos = r > 0 ? 1 : 0; return ctx.state.pos every bar (0 before 90 bars).
rationale: Time-series momentum peaks at the 3-12 month horizon in futures; crypto has only been tested here at the 4-week horizon, so the medium horizon is the open question.
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012, 'Time series momentum', JFE 104(2); Grobys & Sapkota 2019, 'Cryptocurrencies and momentum', Economics Letters 180, 6-10

name: Risk-adjusted time-series momentum: weight by the trailing 1-year Sharpe, vol-targeted (Dudler-Gmuer-Malamud)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, assets = 25 ETFs, eligible if bars > 253. S_i = mean(daily ret over 252)/std(daily ret over 252) * sqrt(252); sig_i = max(0, min(2, S_i))/2 (long-only, in [0,1]). vol_i = std(last 60 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w_i = sig_i * (0.10/vol_i) / N_eligible (vol_i floored at 0.01). If sum(w) > 1 divide all weights by sum(w).
rationale: Sizing trend positions by the risk-adjusted strength of the trend (not just its sign) uses more information per asset and Dudler et al. show it beats plain sign-based TSMOM with lower turnover.
source: Dudler, Gmuer & Malamud 2015, 'Momentum and risk adjustment', Journal of Alternative Investments 18(2), 91-103
prereg_note: prereg: divisor changed from fixed 25 to N_eligible (only 3 ETFs exist 2005-2016), vol floor added.

name: CTA-style MACD ensemble trend (3 EMA pairs, response-shaped), vol-targeted, 25 ETFs (Baz et al.)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, assets = 25 ETFs, eligible if bars > 400. For each asset and each pair (S,L) in {(8,24),(16,48),(32,96)}: x = EMA_S(close) - EMA_L(close) (EMA alpha 2/(n+1), seeded with the SMA of the first n closes); y = x / std(close over last 63 bars); z = y / std(y over last 252 bars); u = z*exp(-z*z/4)/0.89. signal = mean of the three u (in about [-1,1]). sig = max(0, signal) (long-only). vol = std(last 60 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w = sig * (targetVol/vol) / N_eligible; if sum(w) > 1 divide all weights by sum(w).
rationale: This is the canonical published description of how CTAs actually build trend signals (multi-speed EMA crossovers, double-normalised, with a response function that fades extreme readings); it has not been tested on this ETF set.
source: Baz, Granger, Harvey, Le Roux & Sargaison 2015, 'Dissecting investment strategies in the cross section and time series', SSRN 2695101

name: CTA-style MACD ensemble trend, vol-targeted, 18 crypto (Baz et al.)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 400. For each asset and each pair (S,L) in {(8,24),(16,48),(32,96)}: x = EMA_S(close) - EMA_L(close) (EMA alpha 2/(n+1), seeded with the SMA of the first n closes); y = x / std(close over last 63 bars); z = y / std(y over last 252 bars); u = z*exp(-z*z/4)/0.89. signal = mean of the three u (in about [-1,1]). sig = max(0, signal) (long-only). vol = std(last 60 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w = sig * (0.30/vol) / N_eligible; if sum(w) > 1 divide all weights by sum(w).
rationale: Crypto trends are strong but noisy; the response-shaped multi-speed signal is designed to hold through noise and cut exposure when trends go parabolic, which is exactly the crypto failure mode of plain MA rules.
source: Baz, Granger, Harvey, Le Roux & Sargaison 2015, 'Dissecting investment strategies in the cross section and time series', SSRN 2695101

name: CTA-style MACD ensemble trend, vol-targeted, wide US stocks (Baz et al.)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance weekly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 400. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. For each asset and each pair (S,L) in {(8,24),(16,48),(32,96)}: x = EMA_S(close) - EMA_L(close) (EMA alpha 2/(n+1), seeded with the SMA of the first n closes); y = x / std(close over last 63 bars); z = y / std(y over last 252 bars); u = z*exp(-z*z/4)/0.89. signal = mean of the three u (in about [-1,1]). sig = max(0, signal) (long-only). vol = std(last 60 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w = sig * (0.20/vol) / N_eligible; if sum(w) > 1 divide all weights by sum(w). Then cap each weight at 0.05 (no renormalisation after the cap).
rationale: Single-stock trend following is usually judged by crude MA rules; the CTA ensemble is the fair test of whether stock-level trend survives costs.
source: Baz, Granger, Harvey, Le Roux & Sargaison 2015, 'Dissecting investment strategies in the cross section and time series', SSRN 2695101; Wilcox & Crittenden 2005, 'Does trend following work on stocks?'

name: Momentum turning points: slow 12-month + fast 1-month state machine, 25 ETFs (Goulding-Harvey-Mazzoleni)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 25 ETFs, eligible if bars > 253. slow = sign(close[t]/close[t-252] - 1), fast = sign(close[t]/close[t-21] - 1). State weight: Bull (slow>0, fast>0) 1.0; Correction (slow>0, fast<=0) 0.5; Rebound (slow<=0, fast>0) 0.5; Bear (both <=0) 0. w_i = stateWeight_i / N_eligible (sum <= 1 automatically).
rationale: Combining a slow and a fast trend signal into four states captures turning points earlier than a single lookback while avoiding the whipsaw of the fast signal alone; GHM show the 'intermediate' blend dominates both.
source: Goulding, Harvey & Mazzoleni 2023, 'Momentum turning points', Journal of Financial Economics 149(3), 378-406

name: Momentum turning points: slow 12-month + fast 1-month state machine, 18 crypto (Goulding-Harvey-Mazzoleni)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 253. slow = sign(close[t]/close[t-252] - 1), fast = sign(close[t]/close[t-21] - 1). State weight: Bull (slow>0, fast>0) 1.0; Correction (slow>0, fast<=0) 0.5; Rebound (slow<=0, fast>0) 0.5; Bear (both <=0) 0. w_i = stateWeight_i / N_eligible (sum <= 1 automatically).
rationale: Crypto has violent 1-month reversals inside 12-month trends; the four-state rule keeps half exposure through corrections instead of exiting, which is where single-lookback crypto trend rules bleed.
source: Goulding, Harvey & Mazzoleni 2023, 'Momentum turning points', Journal of Financial Economics 149(3), 378-406

name: Volatility-managed sector ETFs: scale each sector by target variance / last-month realised variance (Moreira-Muir)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 11 sectors, eligible if bars > 22. RV_i = variance of the last 21 daily returns * 252. w_i = (1/11) * min(1.5, 0.0225/RV_i). If sum(w) > 1 divide all by sum(w).
rationale: Realised variance forecasts next-month variance but not next-month return, so scaling exposure by 1/variance raises the Sharpe ratio; Moreira and Muir show this for the market and factor portfolios.
source: Moreira & Muir 2017, 'Volatility-managed portfolios', Journal of Finance 72(4), 1611-1644

name: Volatility targeting on credit ETFs (HYG, LQD), 5% target, weekly (Harvey et al. 'impact of volatility targeting')
rule: rank() mode, weekly, assets = HYG LQD, eligible if bars > 22. vol_i = std(last 21 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w_i = min(0.5, 0.5 * 0.05/vol_i).
rationale: Harvey et al. find vol targeting helps most in assets with strong vol clustering and a negative vol-return relation, with credit the clearest case after equities; bonds and commodities gain little.
source: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison & van Hemert 2018, 'The impact of volatility targeting', Journal of Portfolio Management 45(1), 14-33

name: Volatility-managed Treasuries (TLT, IEF): 8% vol target, weekly (falsification test of Moreira-Muir on bonds)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, assets = TLT IEF, eligible if bars > 22. vol_i = std(last 21 daily returns)*sqrt(252). w_i = min(0.5, 0.5 * 0.08/vol_i).
rationale: Harvey et al. report that vol targeting adds little for bonds because bond vol spikes are not followed by low returns; running the same rule on Treasuries tests whether the credit/equity result is specific or generic.
source: Moreira & Muir 2017, JF 72(4); Harvey et al. 2018, 'The impact of volatility targeting', JPM 45(1)

name: Momentum's January reversal: hold 12-1 winners Feb-Dec, 12-1 losers in January (Jegadeesh-Titman)
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. mom = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1. Let m = calendar month of nextSession(t). If m == 1 (the coming month is January): long the BOTTOM 20% by mom; otherwise long the TOP 20% by mom. Equal weight.
rationale: Momentum is reliably negative in January because December tax-loss selling depresses losers which then rebound; JT and Grinblatt-Moskowitz document the January sign flip explicitly.
source: Jegadeesh & Titman 1993, JF 48(1), Table VII; Grinblatt & Moskowitz 2004, 'Predicting stock price movements from past returns: the role of consistency and tax-loss selling', JFE 71(3)
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions.

name: Long-term reversal: buy the bottom quintile by 36-to-13-month-ago return (De Bondt-Thaler)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 757. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. lt = close[t-252]/close[t-756] - 1 (return from 36 months ago to 12 months ago, skipping the momentum year). Long the bottom 20% by lt, equal weight.
rationale: Investors overreact to multi-year bad news; De Bondt and Thaler's 3-year losers beat winners by ~25% over the next 3 years, and Fama-French's long-term reversal factor still carries it.
source: De Bondt & Thaler 1985, 'Does the stock market overreact?', Journal of Finance 40(3), 793-805

name: Crypto long-term reversal: bottom 6 by 52-week return skipping the last 4 weeks, weekly
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 366. lt = close[t-28]/close[t-365] - 1. Long the 6 names with the lowest lt, weight 1/6 (min 3 names).
rationale: If crypto momentum at 1-4 weeks is over-reaction (as LTW's sign pattern suggests) the year-long losers should mean-revert; LTW report no robust long-horizon reversal, so this is a published null worth settling on a different universe.
source: De Bondt & Thaler 1985, JF 40(3); Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, 'Common risk factors in cryptocurrency', JF 77(2)

name: Volume-conditioned weekly reversal: last-week losers only when the week's volume was high (Conrad-Hameed-Niden)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance weekly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 60. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. ret5 = close[t]/close[t-5] - 1. volRatio = sum(volume[t-4..t]) / (sum(volume[t-54..t-5]) / 10). Candidates = eligible names with volRatio > 1. Long the bottom 20% of the FULL eligible count by ret5 drawn from candidates only (if fewer candidates than that, long all candidates with ret5 < 0; cash if none). Equal weight.
rationale: CHN show weekly reversals are concentrated in high-volume securities (liquidity-driven price pressure) while low-volume weeks show continuation; conditioning on volume is what separates the two.
source: Conrad, Hameed & Niden 1994, 'Volume and autocovariances in short-horizon individual security returns', Journal of Finance 49(4), 1305-1329

name: Intraday-return reversal: long the lowest cumulative open-to-close return over the past month (Lou-Polk-Skouras)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 30. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. intra = sum over k = t-20..t of ln(close[k]/open[k]). Long the bottom 20% by intra, equal weight.
rationale: Lou, Polk and Skouras decompose returns into overnight (which persists) and intraday (which reverses); the intraday component is where institutional price pressure and its reversal live, and only the overnight leg has been tested here.
source: Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019, 'A tug of war: overnight versus intraday expected returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213

name: Seasonal reversal: long names with the lowest average return in the OTHER calendar months (Keloharju-Linnainmaa-Nyberg)
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 760. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. Monthly bars M = ctx.resample(universe[sym], '1M') excluding the incomplete last one; need >= 36 complete months. m = calendar month of nextSession(t). other = mean of the monthly returns of the last 36 complete months whose calendar month != m. Long the bottom 20% by other, equal weight. A 'complete' month = any calendar month strictly before the month containing ymd(t) (the month of t is never used).
rationale: KLN show the seasonality premium is the mirror of a 'seasonal reversal': stocks that did well in the other eleven months underperform in month m, so the two legs together explain the Heston-Sadka effect.
source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg 2021, 'Are return seasonalities due to risk or mispricing?', Journal of Financial Economics 139(1), 138-167
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions. prereg: defined 'complete month' (excludes the month of t).

name: Same-weekday return seasonality: long the names with the best average return on the coming weekday over the past year (Keloharju et al.)
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance daily, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 300. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. d = dow(nextSession(t)). For each eligible name take the last 52 bars whose own date has dow == d and average their close-to-close returns (bar k return = close[k]/close[k-1]-1). Long the top 20% by that average, equal weight, rebalanced every bar.
rationale: Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg find return seasonalities at every frequency including the day of the week, with the same-weekday sort earning a significant premium; it has never been tried on this universe.
source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg 2016, 'Return seasonalities', Journal of Finance 71(4), 1557-1590
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions.

name: Day-of-week lottery tilt: short high-vol/long low-vol into Monday, reverse into Friday (Birru)
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance daily, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 70. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. longShort. vol = std of the last 60 daily returns; H = top 20% by vol, L = bottom 20% by vol. If dow(t) == 5 (Friday bar, position held into Monday): weight +0.5/|L| on each L name and -0.5/|H| on each H name. If dow(t) == 4 (Thursday bar, held into Friday): +0.5/|H| on H and -0.5/|L| on L. Any other weekday: all weights 0 (cash).
rationale: Mood is lowest on Mondays and highest on Fridays, and speculative (high-vol) stocks are the most mood-sensitive, so they underperform into Monday and outperform into Friday; Birru finds ~0.3%/week spreads.
source: Birru 2018, 'Day of the week and the cross-section of returns', Journal of Financial Economics 130(1), 182-214
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions.

name: Turn-of-month beta rotation: high beta over month-end days, low beta otherwise (Etula et al. 'Dash for cash')
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance daily, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 260. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). beta_i = cov(ret_i, EW market)/var(EW market) over 252 bars. TOM window: a session is in the window if it is the last session of its calendar month or one of the first 3 sessions of a month (count sessions from universe calendar dates seen so far). Let k = number of universe-calendar sessions seen so far in the month of ymd(t), including t. Use the high-beta quintile if ANY of: (a) nextSession(t) is in a later calendar month than ymd(t) (bar t+1 is session 1); (b) k is 1 or 2 (bar t+1 is session 2 or 3); (c) exactly one weekday lies after ymd(t) in its calendar month (bar t+1 is the last session). Otherwise the low-beta quintile. Equal weight.
rationale: Etula et al. show institutional month-end liquidity needs push risky (high-beta) assets down before month-end and up after, with the effect scaling in beta; rotating beta around the turn captures both legs.
source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen 2020, 'Dash for cash: monthly market impact of institutional liquidity needs', Review of Financial Studies 33(1), 75-111
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions. prereg: TOM decision rewritten as an explicit three-case test.

name: Announcement-day beta: high-beta on employment-report and FOMC days, low-beta otherwise (Savor-Wilson)
rule: Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance daily, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 260. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). beta_i as cov/var over 252 bars. Employment-report day R for calendar month M (BLS rule: the 3rd Friday after the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th): d12 = M-12; sat = d12 + (6 - dow(d12)) days; R = sat + 20 days (always a Friday; e.g. 2024-01 report -> 2024-02-02, 2024-09 -> 2024-10-04). Build the set of all R for every month in the sample a priori. FOMC decision dates = the FOMC_DATES list in research/hunt2/strategies/calendar-fomc-drift.mjs, copied verbatim as a literal array into the strategy file (imports are banned). If nextSession(t) is an employment-report day or an FOMC date: long the top 20% by beta; otherwise long the bottom 20% by beta. Equal weight.
rationale: Savor and Wilson show the CAPM holds on scheduled macro-announcement days (beta is rewarded ~10x more) and fails on all other days, so beta should be owned only on announcement days.
source: Savor & Wilson 2014, 'Asset pricing: a tale of two days', Journal of Financial Economics 113(2), 171-201
prereg_note: prereg: added the shared ymd/dow/nextSession definitions. prereg: FOMC list must be copied as a literal.

name: Employment-report day premium: long QQQ/DIA into the monthly jobs report only (Savor-Wilson)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Employment-report day R for calendar month M (BLS rule: the 3rd Friday after the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th): d12 = M-12; sat = d12 + (6 - dow(d12)) days; R = sat + 20 days (always a Friday; e.g. 2024-01 report -> 2024-02-02, 2024-09 -> 2024-10-04). Build the set of all R for every month in the sample a priori. Return 1 at bar i if ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) is an employment-report day R (so the position is held from the Thursday close through the Friday close); else 0.
rationale: Savor and Wilson find the equity premium is earned almost entirely on scheduled macro-announcement days (employment, CPI, FOMC); the employment report is the only one whose date is a deterministic calendar rule.
source: Savor & Wilson 2013, 'How much do investors care about macroeconomic risk? Evidence from scheduled economic announcements', JFQA 48(2), 343-375

name: Lunar cycle: long QQQ/DIA in the week around the new moon, flat around the full moon (Dichev-Janes)
rule: signal() mode. phase = (((bars[i].time + 86400) - 947182440) / (29.530588853*86400)) mod 1 (phase of the coming session; 0 = new moon, 0.5 = full moon). Return 1 if phase < 0.125 or phase > 0.875 (about 7.4 days centred on the new moon), else 0.
rationale: Dichev and Janes report returns in the 15 days around new moons are about double those around full moons across all major US indices and 24 of 25 countries; a classic widely-asked calendar oddity that deserves a clean costed test.
source: Dichev & Janes 2003, 'Lunar cycle effects in stock returns', Journal of Private Equity 6(4), 8-29; Yuan, Zheng & Zhu 2006, 'Are investors moonstruck?', Journal of Empirical Finance 13(1)

name: First-half-of-month effect: long QQQ/DIA for the first 9 sessions of each month (Ariel)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Track k = number of bars seen so far in the current calendar month, including bar i (reset when the month of ymd changes). Return 1 if k <= 8 (bar i+1 is session 2..9) or if nextSession(t) falls in a new month (bar i+1 is session 1); else 0.
rationale: Ariel found the entire equity premium accrues in the first half of the month (last day of prior month through the 9th session), with the second half flat; the narrow -1..+3 turn-of-month window is tested here, the full half-month is not.
source: Ariel 1987, 'A monthly effect in stock returns', Journal of Financial Economics 18(1), 161-174

name: Month-end Treasury rebalancing: long TLT/IEF/AGG over the last 3 sessions of each month (Etula et al.)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. r = number of weekdays strictly after ymd(t) and still inside the same calendar month. Return 1 if 1 <= r <= 3 (bar i+1 is one of the last 3 sessions), else 0.
rationale: Month-end bond index duration extension and institutional 'dash for cash' flows push Treasury prices up into the last days of the month and leave them flat afterward; Etula et al. document the pattern in Treasuries as well as equities.
source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen 2020, 'Dash for cash', RFS 33(1); Lou, Yan & Zhang 2013, 'Anticipated and repeated shocks in liquid markets', RFS 26(8)

name: Post-expiration week weakness: flat QQQ/DIA for the 5 sessions after the third Friday (Stivers-Sun)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. thirdFri(M) = the 3rd Friday of calendar month M (date 15..21 with dow 5). Position is 0 if nextSession(t) is one of the 5 weekday dates following thirdFri (Mon..Fri of the next week), else 1.
rationale: Stivers and Sun find index returns in the week after monthly option expiration are reliably low (negative on average) as dealer hedging flows unwind; the expiration week itself has been tested here, the following week has not.
source: Stivers & Sun 2013, 'Returns and option activity over the option-expiration cycle for stock-index funds', Journal of Banking & Finance 37(5), 1537-1552

name: Autumn effect in gold: long GLD/SLV only during September and November (Baur)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Return 1 if the calendar month of nextSession(t) is 9 or 11, else 0.
rationale: Baur documents significantly higher gold returns in September and November (Indian wedding/festival demand, hedging into year-end) over 1980-2010; it is the best-known gold seasonal and untested here.
source: Baur 2013, 'The autumn effect of gold price returns', Research in International Business and Finance 27(1), 1-11

name: Seasonal-affective bond demand: long Treasury/aggregate bond ETFs September to November (Kamstra-Kramer-Levi-Wermers)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Return 1 if the calendar month of nextSession(t) is 9, 10 or 11, else 0.
rationale: KKLW show mutual-fund flows rotate into safe assets as daylight shortens in autumn and back into equities in spring, and that Treasury returns are seasonally high over that window.
source: Kamstra, Kramer, Levi & Wermers 2017, 'Seasonal asset allocation: evidence from mutual fund flows', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52(1), 71-109

name: Crypto year-end holiday drift: long all 18 from the Dec 24 close to the Jan 2 close (Kaiser)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Return 1 if ymd(t) is between Dec 24 and Jan 1 inclusive (position held into Dec 25 .. Jan 2 sessions), else 0.
rationale: Kaiser's seasonality study of cryptocurrencies finds calendar effects around year-end; the Santa-window drift is tested on equities here but not on crypto, where thin holiday liquidity could amplify or kill it.
source: Kaiser 2019, 'Seasonality in cryptocurrencies', Finance Research Letters 31, 232-238; Lakonishok & Smidt 1988, 'Are seasonal anomalies real?', RFS 1(4)

name: CME expiry drag: short crypto for the 3 sessions into the last Friday of each month
rule: signal() mode, longShort. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. lastFri(M) = last Friday of calendar month M. Return -1 if ymd(t) is lastFri - 3, lastFri - 2 or lastFri - 1 days (Tue, Wed, Thu bars; positions held through Wed, Thu, Fri), else 0.
rationale: CME bitcoin futures settle on the last Friday; since their 2018 launch BTC has shown a documented tendency to weaken into expiry as hedged basis positions unwind, a pattern reported by the FRBSF and widely watched by traders.
source: Hale, Krishnamurthy, Kudlyak & Shultz 2018, 'How futures trading changed Bitcoin prices', FRBSF Economic Letter 2018-12; Arcane Research 2019, 'Bitcoin and the CME expiry effect'

name: January barometer per sector: hold each sector/index ETF Feb-Dec only if its own January return was positive
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. On every bar whose month is 12 store ctx.state.decClose = close[i]. On a bar whose month is 1 and whose nextSession(t) is in February (the last January bar), set ctx.state.jan = decClose defined && close[i]/ctx.state.decClose - 1 > 0. Return 1 if the month of nextSession(t) is 1 (January is always held); else return ctx.state.jan === true ? 1 : 0 (0 before the first measured January, and 0 for Feb-Dec of a year whose January was negative).
rationale: The 'other January effect' (as January goes, so goes the year) holds in US index data since 1940 and in sectors; Cooper et al. and Stivers et al. show it survives risk and subperiod controls.
source: Cooper, McConnell & Ovtchinnikov 2006, 'The other January effect', JFE 82(2), 315-341; Stivers, Sun & Sun 2009, 'The other January effect: international, style, and subperiod evidence', JFM 12(3)
prereg_note: prereg: January read moved to the last January bar so the first February session uses the current year's barometer; pre-first-January state defined.

name: Halloween effect by sector: cyclicals Nov-Apr, defensives May-Oct (Jacobsen-Visaltanachoti)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. m = calendar month of nextSession(t); winter = m in {11,12,1,2,3,4}. For a cyclical ETF return winter ? 1 : 0; for a defensive ETF return winter ? 0 : 1. The asset is identified by ctx.symbol (exposed by the harness in signal mode).
rationale: Jacobsen and Visaltanachoti show the Sell-in-May effect is concentrated in cyclical/production sectors and absent in consumer-defensive sectors, which argues for rotating rather than exiting.
source: Jacobsen & Visaltanachoti 2009, 'The Halloween effect in US sectors', Financial Review 44(3), 437-459

name: Intraday momentum in crypto: first-hour return predicts the last hour of the UTC day (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou)
rule: signal() mode on 1h bars, longShort. hour(i) = floor(bars[i].time/3600) % 24. When hour(i) == 22: find the bar j <= i with the same UTC date and hour(j) == 0; f = close[j]/open[j] - 1; return f > 0 ? 1 : (f < 0 ? -1 : 0) (0 if no hour-0 bar exists that day) (held over the 23:00-00:00 bar). Every other hour return 0.
rationale: Gao et al. show the first half-hour return of the session predicts the last half-hour (late informed trading and infrequent rebalancers); crypto's 24h UTC day gives a clean analogue with no overnight gap.
source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018, 'Market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 394-414
prereg_note: prereg: missing hour-0 bar case defined.

name: Index-level overnight-return momentum: long QQQ/DIA while the trailing 20-day overnight return is positive
rule: signal() mode. ON = sum over k = i-19..i of ln(open[k]/close[k-1]). Return 1 if ON > 0 else 0 (0 before 21 bars).
rationale: Overnight returns persist (Lou-Polk-Skouras; Cooper-Cliff-Gulen) and carry the bulk of the index premium; using the sign of recent overnight drift as a timing signal tests whether that persistence is tradeable at the index level.
source: Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019, JFE 134(1); Cooper, Cliff & Gulen 2008, 'Return differences between trading and non-trading hours: like night and day', SSRN 1004081

name: Volume trend: long stocks whose monthly volume has been declining over two years (Haugen-Baker)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 540. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. M = ctx.resample(universe[sym], '1M') complete months, last 24. OLS slope b of monthly volume on month index 1..24; vt = b / mean(monthly volume). Long the bottom 20% by vt (most negative trend), equal weight. A 'complete' month = any calendar month strictly before the month containing ymd(t) (the month of t is never used).
rationale: Rising volume marks attention and speculative demand that fades; Haugen and Baker find volume trend among the strongest negative predictors of return, and Chen-Zimmermann's replication keeps it significant.
source: Haugen & Baker 1996, 'Commonality in the determinants of expected stock returns', Journal of Financial Economics 41(3), 401-439 ('VolumeTrend' in Chen & Zimmermann 2022 open-source asset pricing)
prereg_note: prereg: defined 'complete month' (excludes the month of t).

name: High-low bid-ask spread estimator: long the most illiquid quintile by Corwin-Schultz spread
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 30. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. For each consecutive pair of days (k-1,k) in the last 21 bars: beta = ln(H[k-1]/L[k-1])^2 + ln(H[k]/L[k])^2; gamma = ln(max(H[k-1],H[k])/min(L[k-1],L[k]))^2; alpha = (sqrt(2*beta) - sqrt(beta))/(3 - 2*sqrt(2)) - sqrt(gamma/(3 - 2*sqrt(2))); S = 2*(exp(alpha)-1)/(1+exp(alpha)), floored at 0. spread = mean S over the 20 pairs. Long the top 20% by spread, equal weight.
rationale: The Corwin-Schultz estimator recovers the effective spread from daily highs and lows; a spread/illiquidity premium is one of the oldest cross-sectional effects (Amihud-Mendelson) and this is the only price-only spread measure.
source: Corwin & Schultz 2012, 'A simple way to estimate bid-ask spreads from daily high and low prices', Journal of Finance 67(2), 719-760; Amihud & Mendelson 1986, JFE 17(2)

name: Sector residual momentum: rank sectors by the Sharpe of their market-residual return over months 12-2 (Blitz-Huij-Martens)
rule: rank() mode, monthly, assets = 11 sectors, eligible if bars > 253. Market = equal-weight mean of the 11 sectors' daily returns. For each sector regress its daily returns on market over the last 252 bars (OLS alpha, beta); residual e_k = r_k - alpha - beta*mkt_k. score = mean(e over k = t-251..t-21)/std(e over the same window). Long the top 3 by score, 1/3 each.
rationale: Residual momentum keeps the stock-specific continuation and strips the market-factor exposure that causes momentum crashes; Blitz et al. report half the volatility and similar returns to total-return momentum.
source: Blitz, Huij & Martens 2011, 'Residual momentum', Journal of Empirical Finance 18(3), 506-521

name: Acceleration: long stocks whose last-6-month return most exceeds the prior 6 months (Ardila-Alvarez-Forro-Sornette)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. acc = (close[t]/close[t-126] - 1) - (close[t-126]/close[t-252] - 1). Long the top 20% by acc, equal weight.
rationale: The change in momentum (second derivative of log price) predicts returns beyond momentum itself because investors extrapolate changes in trend; the authors report a significant 'gamma' premium in US stocks.
source: Ardila-Alvarez, Forro & Sornette 2021, 'The acceleration effect and gamma factor in asset pricing', Physica A 569, 125367 (first circulated 2015, Swiss Finance Institute WP 15-30)

name: Crypto on US employment-report day: long all 18 for the UTC session of the jobs report (Corbet et al.)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Employment-report day R for calendar month M (BLS rule: the 3rd Friday after the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th): d12 = M-12; sat = d12 + (6 - dow(d12)) days; R = sat + 20 days (always a Friday; e.g. 2024-01 report -> 2024-02-02, 2024-09 -> 2024-10-04). Build the set of all R for every month in the sample a priori. Return 1 at bar i if ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) is an employment-report day R (held over the UTC day containing the 13:30 UTC release); else 0.
rationale: Corbet et al. find bitcoin reacts significantly to US employment and inflation news; if the Savor-Wilson announcement premium is a global risk-compensation effect it should show in crypto too.
source: Corbet, Larkin, Lucey, Meegan & Yarovaya 2020, 'The impact of macroeconomic news on Bitcoin returns', European Journal of Finance 26(14), 1396-1416; Savor & Wilson 2013, JFQA 48(2)

name: Crypto momentum crash gate: 3-week cross-sectional momentum scaled down after a bear year with high vol (Daniel-Moskowitz in crypto)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 366. mom = close[t]/close[t-21] - 1; pick the top k = max(3, floor(0.3*N_eligible)) (cash if N_eligible < 3). EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of eligible daily returns. bear = cumulative EW market return over the last 365 days < 0; highVol = std(last 30 EW market daily returns)*sqrt(365) > 0.8. s = 1 / 0.5 / 0 for neither / one / both. Weight = s/N on each pick.
rationale: Momentum crashes happen in the rebound after bear markets when vol is high; crypto's 2019 and 2023 rebounds are exactly such states, so the Daniel-Moskowitz gate is a natural fix for the crypto momentum tested here.
source: Daniel & Moskowitz 2016, 'Momentum crashes', JFE 122(2); Grobys & Sapkota 2019, 'Cryptocurrencies and momentum', Economics Letters 180
prereg_note: prereg: 'min 3' made explicit.

name: Crypto residual momentum: BTC-beta-adjusted 4-week return (skip 3 days) scaled by residual vol, weekly
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 181 (BTCUSDT required as the factor). For each alt regress its daily returns on BTC's over the last 180 bars (OLS alpha, beta); residual e. score = sum(e over k = t-27..t-3) / std(e over the 180-bar window). BTC is the factor only and is never scored or held. Long the top 5 alts by score, 1/5 each (cash if fewer than 3 alts eligible).
rationale: Most alt momentum is just BTC beta; the residual (coin-specific) component has lower vol and, by Blitz-Huij-Martens' logic, should carry the continuation without the beta-driven crashes.
source: Blitz, Huij & Martens 2011, 'Residual momentum', Journal of Empirical Finance 18(3); Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, JF 77(2)
prereg_note: prereg: BTC handling simplified (factor only, never held).

name: Tail-risk beta: long the quintile whose returns load most on innovations in cross-sectional tail risk (Kelly-Jiang)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 540. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. Each complete calendar month m (from universe calendar): pool all eligible names' daily returns in m; u = the 5th percentile of the pool; lambda_m = mean over pooled returns r < u of ln(r/u) (Hill estimator on the lower tail). Innovation d_m = lambda_m - lambda_(m-1). For each name with >= 24 monthly returns: beta_i = cov(monthly return_i, d)/var(d) over the last 24 months. Long the top 20% by beta_i, equal weight. A 'complete' month = any calendar month strictly before the month containing ymd(t) (the month of t is never used).
rationale: Kelly and Jiang find stocks with high sensitivity to aggregate tail-risk innovations earn a ~5%/yr premium as compensation for crash exposure; the measure needs only the cross-section of daily returns.
source: Kelly & Jiang 2014, 'Tail risk and asset prices', Review of Financial Studies 27(10), 2841-2871
prereg_note: prereg: defined 'complete month' (excludes the month of t).

name: Momentum among high-volatility stocks: 12-1 winners within the top half by volatility (Bandarchuk-Hilscher)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 260. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. vol = std of daily returns over 252 bars. H = top 50% of eligible names by vol. Among H, long the names with the highest close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1, taking 0.2*N_eligible names. Equal weight.
rationale: Bandarchuk and Hilscher show momentum profits scale with the extremeness of the stock's past return, which is mechanically larger in high-vol names; this is the opposite sort to the 'exclude high idio-risk' version tested here.
source: Bandarchuk & Hilscher 2013, 'Beyond the gap: momentum and extreme characteristics', Review of Finance 17(2), 809-845

name: Crypto conservative formula: lowest-vol half, then top 4 by 12-week momentum, weekly (Blitz-van Vliet in crypto)
rule: rank() mode, weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, eligible if bars > 91. vol = std of the last 90 daily returns; H = the lowest-vol half (floor(N/2) names). Among H, long the top k = min(4, |H|) by close[t-7]/close[t-84] - 1, weight 1/k each; cash if k < 3.
rationale: Pure low-vol crypto baskets fill with dead coins; adding a momentum sort inside the low-vol half is the conservative-formula fix and tests whether low-vol-plus-trend is the part that transfers from equities.
source: Blitz & van Vliet 2018, 'The conservative formula', Journal of Portfolio Management 44(7); Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, JF 77(2)
prereg_note: prereg: 'min 3' made explicit.

name: Liquidity beta: long stocks whose returns rise most when aggregate illiquidity improves (Pastor-Stambaugh, price-volume proxy)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 540. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. Daily Amihud for name j: a_j = |ret_j| / (close_j * volume_j). Aggregate L_d = cross-sectional mean of a_j over eligible names; monthly L_m = mean of L_d in month m (universe calendar). Liquidity innovation u_m = -(ln L_m - ln L_(m-1)) (positive = liquidity improved). For each name with >= 24 monthly returns: beta_i = cov(monthly return_i, u)/var(u) over the last 36 months. Long the top 20% by beta_i, equal weight. A 'complete' month = any calendar month strictly before the month containing ymd(t) (the month of t is never used).
rationale: Pastor and Stambaugh show stocks whose returns covary with market-wide liquidity shocks earn a ~7.5%/yr premium; the proxy here replaces their order-flow measure with the Amihud ratio, which is price-volume only.
source: Pastor & Stambaugh 2003, 'Liquidity risk and expected stock returns', Journal of Political Economy 111(3), 642-685; Amihud 2002, JFM 5(1)
prereg_note: prereg: defined 'complete month' (excludes the month of t).

name: Weekly-return momentum with a one-week skip: twelve overlapping one-week cohorts (Gutierrez-Kelley)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance weekly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 80. Default weights: equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); gross sum <= 1. Any explicit weight formula below overrides this default. At weekly rebalance t, for k = 2..13 let tk = t - 5*k. Cohort k = top 20% of eligible names by close[tk]/close[tk-5] - 1 (ranked with bars up to tk only). Weight(sym) = sum over k of (1/12)*(1/Nk) for each cohort containing sym.
rationale: Gutierrez and Kelley show weekly winners reverse for one week and then outperform for the following year, so skipping one week converts the weekly reversal into long-lasting momentum.
source: Gutierrez & Kelley 2008, 'The long-lasting momentum in weekly returns', Journal of Finance 63(1), 415-447
